plotSections.title: The Keystone Keepers
bullets: Ord chooses Feldspar and receives its keystone, becoming responsible for protecting the realm's knowledge, magic, alchemy, and experimentation.

Ciri chooses Lith as her realm to protect. Lith officially rejects or dismisses magic as folklore and superstition, despite possessing magic themselves; supernatural events occasionally appear there and become the basis for cryptid legends.
With Ciri's choice, all six party members have selected keystones: Gerk–Midgard, Sylan–Gilbrick, Dana–Pitel, Walker–The Reach, Ord–Feldspar, and Ciri–Lith.

There are eight keystones but only six current keepers. The two remaining keystones, for Turof and La-rel, will remain under the stewardship of Kit Anger and the DM/Navi until future keepers can take up those mantles.
The party is formally recognized as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree and honorary members of the Navi. Gerk is specifically designated the Doorman, while the other five are Gatekeepers.

The gods emphasize that the party's new responsibility is especially dangerous because the lich they have been trying to find is seeking the same powerful objects they have now been entrusted to protect.

plotSections.title: Gerk's Doorman Power
bullets: Gerk discovers that his role as the Doorman allows him to open an invisible door by reaching forward, finding an unseen handle, and pulling it open.
The door does not create a conventional threshold; it appears as reality itself being peeled or bent back, revealing the destination seamlessly.
Gerk's first attempt opens onto a beach somewhere on Midgard at sunset, complete with gulls, salt air, and a sea breeze.
The exact destination of Gerk's door cannot yet be deliberately selected; even the DM does not know precisely where the first door leads.

Sylan attempts to use his keystone to interact with a similar doorway but only briefly senses something before the connection disappears, suggesting the keystones and Gerk's Doorman ability function differently.

plotSections.title: The Two Unkept Arches
bullets: The party is reminded that Turof and La-rel must not be forgotten despite lacking dedicated keepers.
Kit Anger and the DM will act as stewards for those two keystones until two future individuals take up the mantles.
The distinction between Gerk's Doorman role and the others' Gatekeeper roles is emphasized: Gerk appears to have a unique ability to physically open doors between places or realms.

plotSections.title: The Child of the Tree
bullets: The party's status as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree is formally confirmed as part of becoming keystone keepers.
The DM explains that the party's discovery of Gerk as the Child of the Tree was connected to the Mother’s Prayer, with the Stranger/Narul having identified or communicated this connection to the DM.
The gods acknowledge that the party's new responsibilities may be part of events that fate requires to happen, even though the consequences are uncertain.

chronologicalEvents: Ord chooses Feldspar and receives its keystone.
Ciri returns and is told she must choose one of the remaining keystones: La-rel, Turof, or Lith.
The DM explains that Lith rejects magic culturally, though magic still exists there and supernatural occurrences occasionally inspire cryptid legends.
Ciri chooses Lith and receives its keystone.
The DM reveals that there are eight keystones but only six current party keepers, leaving Turof and La-rel without dedicated keepers.
Kit Anger and the DM agree to steward the Turof and La-rel keystones until future keepers can take up those mantles.
The party is formally recognized as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree and honorary members of the Navi.
Gerk is distinguished as the Doorman while the other party members are Gatekeepers.
Gerk demonstrates the Doorman ability by opening an invisible door that bends reality and reveals a beach somewhere on Midgard.
Sylan attempts to interact with a doorway using his keystone but only briefly senses something before the connection disappears.
The DM warns that the party now has responsibility for powerful keystones that the lich they have been pursuing is also seeking.
The group prepares to end the council with the gods, with Walker asking whether there is anything further to learn about Grixto.
Vecna indicates that he needs to find a book before the meeting can fully conclude.

quotesThemes: Chooses Lith because it sounds like an interesting place to protect.

quotesThemes: Lith's rejection of magic does not mean that magic is absent from the realm.
